newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Former HK customs boss faces trial for smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Former HK customs boss faces trial for smuggling.

text.p: A former Hong Kong chief customs officer charged with spiriting stolen cars into China will be the first person to stand trial in the territory after Britain hands the colony back to China in July.
A court on Tuesday ordered Chan Tay-wah, 56, to be tried on July 3 on charges of smuggling stolen vehicles into China, Hong Kong's Independent Commission Against Corruption said in a statement.
The retired chief customs officer, charged by the ICAC with a total of six offences, has entered a not guilty plea.
Britain returns Hong Kong to China on July 1, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule but retaining Hong Kong's common law legal system.
July 1 and 2 will be public holidays to mark the occasion and the courts will be closed.
